text:
Alex Morgan, a dedicated QA/Test Engineer at AdVerve Solutions, based in Tel Aviv, Israel, brings a focused approach to quality assurance within the adtech industry. With two years of hands-on experience, Alex has developed a keen understanding of testing methodologies and automation tools, contributing to the reliability and performance of ad-serving platforms. A graduate of the State University of Technology with a Bachelor of Science in Computer Science (2022), Alex’s academic foundation in software development has been complemented by practical experience in a small enterprise environment, fostering adaptability and problem-solving skills.  

During the past 18 months, Alex has evolved from a Software Intern at AdVerve Solutions to a Test Engineer, working closely with cross-functional teams to ensure the accuracy and scalability of ad-tech systems. As an intern, Alex assisted in debugging ad-serving APIs, identifying edge cases in campaign management workflows, and documenting test scenarios for legacy systems. This role laid the groundwork for a deeper engagement with automation, leading to a year as a QA Automation Specialist. Here, Alex developed Selenium test scripts to validate the functionality of campaign management dashboards, ensuring alignment with business requirements. The ability to translate user stories into automated test cases became a core part of the workflow, reducing manual testing efforts by approximately 30% in the modules under responsibility.  

In the most recent role as Test Engineer, Alex focused on integration testing for real-time bidding modules, collaborating with backend developers to resolve synchronization issues between ad inventory and bidding algorithms. This involved designing test scenarios to simulate high-traffic environments, ensuring system stability under load. The role also introduced exposure to CI/CD pipelines, where Alex integrated test scripts into GitLab CI pipelines, enabling automated regression testing for critical features. This practice reduced deployment-related bugs by 25%, as measured by the team’s defect tracking system.  

Alex’s technical toolkit includes Python, used to script data validation routines for API responses, and Selenium/Playwright for browser-based functional testing. A foundational understanding of REST API design has been applied in validating endpoints for ad delivery services, ensuring compliance with industry standards. While Java is occasionally referenced in discussions about system architecture, its direct application remains limited to foundational knowledge. Similarly, microservices architecture is mentioned in the context of distributed testing challenges, though practical experience with such systems is still in development.  

Performance testing tools like JMeter and k6 are listed in the skills section, with limited direct usage due to the team’s focus on functional and integration testing. However, Alex has contributed to preliminary load testing efforts for ad-serving APIs, identifying bottlenecks in request-response cycles. Unit testing, though not a primary focus, has been practiced in smaller-scale projects, such as validating utility functions for test data generation.  

Alex’s work at AdVerve Solutions has emphasized collaboration, precision, and continuous improvement. The ability to adapt to evolving requirements in a fast-paced adtech environment, combined with a commitment to thorough testing, has positioned Alex as a reliable contributor to the team’s quality goals. While there is room for growth in areas like performance optimization and advanced automation, the foundation laid through these experiences continues to support meaningful contributions to the organization’s technical objectives.
